On the controller

Closed loop on the controller

SPARKTalon
ModesPosition, velocity, current, MAXMotionPosition, velocity, Motion Magic, in volts or duty cycle
Loop rateEvery 1 ms1 kHz, so also every 1 ms
FeedforwardkS, kV, kA, plus an arbitrary term from your codekS, kV, kA, plus a FeedForward term in the request
GravitykG for elevators. kCos with kCosRatio for armskG with GravityType. GravityArmPositionOffset shifts the arm angle
Gain slots4, chosen in setSetpoint3, plus simple gain scheduling on error
Arrived?isAtSetpoint()ClosedLoopError, and MotionMagicAtTarget for the profile
Followingconfig.follow(leader, invert), set on the followerFollower request: copies the leader’s output type

Arm gravity works the same way on both: the sensor must read 0 when the arm is level.

Deck 7 · REV vs CTRE

6

On the controller

Motion profiles on the controller

MAXMotion (REV)

Position: a trapezoid. Speed up, cruise, slow down.

You set cruise velocity, max acceleration and allowed profile error.

Drift too far off the plan and the SPARK makes a new plan from where it is.

Velocity: ramps to a speed at your max acceleration.

Motion Magic (CTRE)

Motion Magic: a trapezoid, or a smoother S-curve if you set jerk.

Velocity: ramps to a speed at your acceleration, with optional jerk.

Expo: an exponential curve from kV and kA that fits what the motor can do.

Dynamic: change the limits in every request. Needs Pro and a CANivore.

Deck 7 · REV vs CTRE

7

On the controller

Limits and protection

SPARKTalon
Motor currentSmart Current Limit. Holds phase current. Default 80 AStator limit. Default 120 A, on
Battery currentNo separate settingSupply limit. Default 70 A, then 40 A after 1 s, on
Soft limitsForward and reverse, in softLimitForward and reverse, in SoftwareLimitSwitch. Position targets get capped to them
Limit switchesWired to the data portTalon FXS: wired. Kraken X60: none, so use a CANcoder, CANdi or CANrange
Battery sagvoltageCompensation holds output steadyVoltage requests do this, up to what the battery gives

Brownout is the same on both. Below 6.3 V (roboRIO 1) or 6.75 V (roboRIO 2 default), the roboRIO sends CAN motor controllers an explicit disable.

Deck 7 · REV vs CTRE

8

Best practice

Run the loop on the controller, limit every motor

If timing matters, run the loop on the controller. On every motor, set a current limit.

The controller reads a wired sensor directly, every millisecond. And the 80 A SPARK default is twice the top of REV’s suggested range for a NEO 550, which is 20 A to 40 A.

// SPARK

config.smartCurrentLimit(40);

// Talon FX

config.CurrentLimits.StatorCurrentLimit = 40;

config.CurrentLimits.StatorCurrentLimitEnable = true;

Deck 7 · REV vs CTRE

9

Cost

Free features and paid features

Without Pro, a request with EnableFOC falls back to normal drive, but TorqueCurrentFOC will not run. A Season Pass covers 100 devices for one team number. Pro features are free in simulation.

REV: one tier

REVLib, Hardware Client 2, StatusLogger, MAXMotion and simulation. REV’s docs list no paid software.

Phoenix 6: free

Volt and duty cycle closed loops. Motion Magic, Velocity and Expo. Swerve API. Tuner X. Simulation. Limited log export.

CANivore: hardware

A second CAN bus for CTRE devices, with CAN FD and CANivore timestamps.

Pro license

FOC and torque control on Talon FX. FOC gives about 15% more peak power. FusedCANcoder, SyncCANcoder, full log export, hoot replay.

Pro and CANivore

Timesync, device timestamps, Dynamic Motion Magic, full differential control.

Same job, both vendors

Arm setup: sensor, gains and gravity

REVLib 2026

config.absoluteEncoder

    .apply(AbsoluteEncoderConfig.Presets

        .REV_ThroughBoreEncoderV2)

    .zeroOffset(ENCODER_OFFSET_ROT);

 

config.closedLoop

    .feedbackSensor(

        FeedbackSensor.kAbsoluteEncoder)

    .p(KP)

    .feedForward

    .kV(KV)

    .kCos(KG).kCosRatio(1.0);

Phoenix 6 2026

var feedback = config.Feedback;

feedback.FeedbackRemoteSensorID = ENCODER_ID;

feedback.FeedbackSensorSource =

    FeedbackSensorSourceValue.RemoteCANcoder;

feedback.SensorToMechanismRatio = 1.0;

feedback.RotorToSensorRatio = GEAR_RATIO;

 

config.Slot0.GravityType =

    GravityTypeValue.Arm_Cosine;

config.Slot0.kG = KG;

config.Slot0.kP = KP;

config.Slot0.kV = KV;

Deck 7 · REV vs CTRE

12

Same job, both vendors

Arm move: profile and command

REVLib 2026

config.closedLoop.maxMotion

    .cruiseVelocity(CRUISE_RPM)

    .maxAcceleration(ACCEL_RPM_PER_S)

    .allowedProfileError(PROFILE_ERROR_ROT);

 

public Command moveTo(double degrees) {

  double rotations = degrees / 360.0;

  return runOnce(() -> {

    target = rotations;

    controller.setSetpoint(rotations,

      ControlType.kMAXMotionPositionControl);

  }).andThen(waitUntil(this::atTarget));

}

Phoenix 6 2026

var magic = config.MotionMagic;

magic.MotionMagicCruiseVelocity = CRUISE_RPS;

magic.MotionMagicAcceleration = ACCEL_RPS2;

 

public Command moveTo(double degrees) {

  double rotations = degrees / 360.0;

  return runOnce(() -> {

    target = rotations;

    motor.setControl(

        request.withPosition(rotations));

  }).andThen(waitUntil(this::atTarget));

}

Common mistake

Newest firmware is not always the right firmware

What you see

A SPARK shows “Outdated REV Device”, REVLib says the firmware is too old or too new, or Phoenix reports a firmware version error.

Why it happens

On both vendors, firmware and library are a matched pair for each season. The newest firmware listed can be for next season.

The fix

For 2026, pick the newest 26.x in Hardware Client 2, and the 2026 firmware year in Tuner X.

Deck 7 · REV vs CTRE

14

Decision

How a young team can choose

Budget

Count whole systems. A Kraken includes its controller. A NEO needs a SPARK, and a Minion needs a Talon FXS.

What you own

Start from your shelf. KitBot SPARK MAX controllers, NEO V1.1 and Falcon 500 are all still legal.

Who can help

Choose what your team, or a team nearby, can debug at an event.

Mixing is allowed

R504 lists both vendors and one project can use both libraries. You pay with two apps and two update routines.

Exercise

Pick the parts for one mechanism

1.

Choose one mechanism: an arm, a shooter or an intake.

2.

Pick a motor and a controller. Check them on the pairing table.

3.

Write down its current limit and where its sensor plugs in.

4.

Open RevArm.java or CtreArm.java and find the gravity lines.

Done when: you have a motor, a controller, a current limit and a sensor, and have found the gravity lines.

What changes for 2027

In 2026Changing for 2027
SPARK firmware 26.x, conversion factorsShipped already: firmware 27.0.0, conversion factors gone
Phoenix firmware for 2026Alpha: Phoenix 26.70 needs 26.70.x firmware, no roboRIO
new TalonFX(id, bus) on a roboRIOAlpha: int and String constructors go. CANBus takes a CANPort
new SparkMax(id, type)Alpha: constructors take a WPILib CANPort
